song.title: Break on Through (To the Other Side)

tone.target: raw 60s garage fuzz with biting upper mids
tone.profile: raw 60s garage fuzz with biting upper mids
tone.summary: A raw 60s garage sound achieved using Fuzz and an early British amp model (UK 45/UK 50) paired with a compact cab, emphasizing midrange bite and controlled breakup.
corrections: make verses mostly dry, not clean arpeggios

rig.name: The Doors - Break on Through (To the Other Side) - Valeton GP-180

blocks.purpose: Clean up stray noise inherent in raw fuzz tones.
Slightly push the signal into the fuzz stage for maximum aggression.
blocks.gap: Using Boost instead of OD/Green OD to maintain raw, non-overdriven grit.

alternatives.reason: Could provide more color but might soften the aggressive fuzz edge.

blocks.purpose: Generate the core raw 60s garage fuzz tone.
Simulate a small, cranked British combo amp for tight low end and midrange bite.
blocks.gap: The UK 50 is also viable, but the UK 45 often captures that raw, punchy early 60s sound better.

alternatives.reason: A good alternative for a similar British tone.

blocks.purpose: Provide a compact, punchy cabinet sound that complements the small combo amp model.
blocks.gap: The US 2x12 is too clean; the UK Basket provides necessary grit and size.

alternatives.reason: Too modern/clean for this raw garage sound.
